title: 第65章 实验室里的贵宾第66章 苏木槿的歉意
lines: 秦川在百草谷的头三天，过得比他预想的要平静。
没有人来审问他，没有人来试探他的底细，甚至没有弟子主动来找他说话。他在药田里遇到的人会礼貌地点头致意，然后就低下头继续干活。这种态度不像敌意，倒更像是——他们在等什么。也许是在等谷主的态度进一步明确，也许是在等苏木槿先表态。
第四天，苏木槿给他安排了一间工作间——就在客舍旁边，原本是一间存放草药的库房，被清理出来，摆了一张长桌、几个药柜、一套基础的研药工具。秦川将孙老六的防疫记录和李神医的医案展开在桌上，开始整理一份系统性的凡人医疗手册大纲。
下午，苏木槿带着一个女弟子来见他。女弟子看起来二十出头，面容清秀，眼神很亮，但嘴唇紧抿，一副不太情愿的样子。她穿着百草谷弟子统一的淡绿色长裙，腰间挂着一枚药囊，药囊上绣着两片叶子——秦川从之前观察到的细节中已经了解到，这是丹堂弟子的标记。两片叶子代表中级弟子，一片是初级，三片是高级。中级，意味着已经可以独立开方，但还没有带徒弟的资格。
“这是沈青黛，丹堂的弟子，谷主让她来配合你的研究。”苏木槿的语气很平淡，但秦川注意到她介绍时特意说了“谷主让她来”，这是在给沈青黛一个台阶——不是自愿来的，是奉命来的。
沈青黛行了个礼，动作标准，但眼神一直飘向窗外，明显心不在焉。
“沈姑娘，”秦川直接开口，“你在丹堂主要负责哪方面的研究？”
“丹药的灵力浓度配比。”她的语气公事公办，像在读一份自己都没兴趣的报告。
“那你对凡人用药有什么了解？”
“凡人用药？凡人不需要配比。他们的经脉承受不住灵淬，用灵药等于毒药。所以凡人生病，我们通常给他们开安神散——安抚一下，减缓痛苦。能不能好，看他们自己的命。”
秦川沉默了一瞬。不是愤怒，是共鸣。他想起了地球上的某些医疗理念——对治不了的病人，给点安慰剂，然后看命。这不是残忍，是体系到极限后的无奈。
“沈姑娘，如果你愿意，我想请你帮一个忙。”他说，“把你认为‘对凡人无效’的药材列个清单给我。我想试试能不能找到一些用法——不经过灵淬，直接用凡人的方式处理，也许能发挥不同的效果。”
沈青黛终于转过头正眼看他。那眼神里有一种微妙的变化——不是敌意，而是一个习惯了研究灵丹的丹堂弟子，忽然听到一个她从来没想过的问题时，本能产生的好奇。
“凡人的方式？你是说煎汤？”
“不只是煎汤。还有浸泡、熏蒸、外敷、药浴——很多方法。灵淬是用灵力把药性‘提’出来，但凡人没有灵力。凡人只能用温度、时间、溶媒——也就是水、酒、醋——来萃取药性。方法不同，但目标一样。”
沈青黛沉默了一会儿，然后开口：“我列清单可以。但你别抱太大希望——大部分灵药对凡人的体质都太猛烈。”
“没关系。我们一个一个试。”
沈青黛点了下头，转身走了。她走到门口时停了一下，回过头来，像是想问什么，但最终没有开口，只是又行了个礼，然后匆匆离去。
秦川看着她的背影，微微一笑。他知道那种欲言又止是什么——是一个专业研究者遇到了一个自己从未考虑过的问题，想继续追问却又怕显得太急切。沈青黛是第一个被好奇心驱动的弟子，但不会是最后一个。
苏木槿走过来，轻声说：“沈青黛是丹堂长老的外孙女。她在丹堂的配比研究很出色，但因为研究的是对凡人无效的领域，一直没有得到重视。你刚才说的话，她回去大概会想很久。”
秦川点了点头，在自己的工作簿上写下第一行备注：“沈青黛——灵力浓度配比——可能成为凡人用药研发的对接人。”
写完他放下笔，看着窗外的药田。那些郁郁葱葱的药材在阳光下摇曳，每一株都蕴含着修士们无法完全释放的可能性。他的工作，不是从零开始创造，而是把这些可能性，翻译成凡人也能使用的语言。信息差的本质不是炫耀知识，而是填补盲区。他在百草谷的价值，不在于是苏木槿的客人，不在于是轮回剑主的记名弟子——而在于他能看到别人看不到的盲区，并且愿意去填。
傍晚，沈青黛回来了。她手里捧着一本厚厚的册子，封面上写着《凡人禁忌药材名录》。她把册子放在秦川桌上，面无表情地说：“这是我整理的。所有已知对凡人无效或有毒的灵药。一共二百一十七味。分类按部位、性味、毒性等级排好了。”
秦川翻开册子，看到每一味药材都用工整的小楷写明了名称、性味、归经、毒性和禁忌原因，旁边还用小字注明了具体病例。这份工作的细致程度完全不像一个“奉命应付”的弟子能做到的。
他抬头看着沈青黛。沈青黛偏过头去，耳朵尖微微发红。
“谢谢。”
“不用谢。我只是不想被你乱试药害死人。”她顿了顿，又说，“你有进展可以叫我。”
然后她转身走了。秦川看着她的背影消失在药田间的小径上，又低头看了看手里的册子。二百一十七味药，每一味都写得清清楚楚。这不是敷衍，是一个专业药师被触动了那根名为“这个问题我居然没想过”的神经之后，本能爆发的专业素养。
他合上册子，在工作簿上又加了一行备注：“沈青黛——可用。需求：被认可。痛点：研究领域长期边缘化。突破口：给她一个能被看见的成果。”
content_en:
Qin Chuan's first three days in Baicao Valley were calmer than he expected.
No one came to interrogate him, no one came to test his background, and no disciples even took the initiative to talk to him. People he met in the medicine fields would nod politely, then put their heads down and get back to work. This attitude is not like hostility, but more like - what are they waiting for. Perhaps he was waiting for the Valley Master's attitude to be further clarified, or perhaps he was waiting for Su Mujin to express his stance first.
On the fourth day, Su Mujin arranged a workshop for him - right next to the guest house. It was originally a warehouse for storing medicinal herbs. It was cleared out and equipped with a long table, several medicine cabinets, and a set of basic medicine grinding tools. Qin Chuan spread out Sun Laoliu's epidemic prevention records and Doctor Li's medical records on the table, and began to compile an outline of a systematic medical manual for mortals.
In the afternoon, Su Mujin brought a female disciple to see him. The female disciple looked to be in her early twenties, with a delicate face and bright eyes, but her lips were pressed tightly together, looking reluctant. She was wearing a light green dress uniformly worn by the disciples of Baicao Valley, and hung a medicine pouch on her waist. The medicine pouch was embroidered with two leaves - Qin Chuan had learned from the details he had observed before that this was the mark of a disciple of the Alchemy Hall. Two leaves represent intermediate disciples, one is junior and three is senior. Intermediate level means that you can prescribe independently, but you are not yet qualified to lead an apprentice.
"This is Shen Qingdai, a disciple of Dantang. The Valley Master asked her to cooperate with your research." Su Muxin's tone was very calm, but Qin Chuan noticed that she specifically said "The Valley Master asked her to come" when introducing her. This was to give Shen Qingdai a step up - she did not come voluntarily, but came under orders.
Shen Qingdai saluted, her movements were standard, but her eyes kept drifting to the window, obviously absent-minded.
"Miss Shen," Qin Chuan said directly, "What research area are you mainly responsible for in the Alchemy Hall?"
"The spiritual power concentration ratio of the elixir." Her tone was businesslike, as if she was reading a report that she was not interested in.
"Then what do you know about the use of medicine by mortals?"
"Mortals use medicine? Mortals don't need to mix. Their meridians can't withstand spiritual quenching, and using elixir is equivalent to poison. So when mortals are sick, we usually prescribe Anshen Powder to them - to soothe them and relieve the pain. Whether they can recover or not depends on their own fate."
Qin Chuan was silent for a moment. Not anger, but empathy. He thought of some of the medical concepts on Earth - give a placebo to patients who cannot be cured, and then check their fate. This is not cruelty, but helplessness after the system reaches its limit.
"Miss Shen, if you are willing, I would like to ask you to do a favor." He said, "Make a list of the medicinal materials that you think are 'ineffective for mortals'. I want to see if I can find some ways to use them - without spiritual tempering, directly processing them in a mortal way, which may have different effects."
Shen Qingdai finally turned her head and looked at him. There was a subtle change in the eyes - not hostility, but the instinctive curiosity of a Dan Hall disciple who was used to studying spiritual elixirs, and suddenly heard a question she had never thought of.
"The mortal way? You mean decoction?"
"It's not just decoction. There are also soaking, fumigation, topical application, medicinal baths - many methods. Spiritual quenching uses spiritual power to 'extract' the medicinal properties, but mortals don't have spiritual power. Mortals can only use temperature, time, and solvents - that is, water, wine, vinegar - to extract the medicinal properties. The methods are different, but the goal is the same."
Shen Qingdai was silent for a while, and then said: "I can make a list. But don't have high hopes - most of the elixirs are too strong for mortal bodies."
"It doesn't matter. Let's try them one by one."
Shen Qingdai nodded, turned and left. When she reached the door, she paused, turned around, as if she wanted to ask something, but in the end she didn't speak, she just saluted again, and then left in a hurry.
Qin Chuan looked at her back and smiled slightly. He knew what it was like to be hesitant to speak - it was when a professional researcher encountered a problem he had never considered and wanted to continue asking but was afraid of appearing too eager. Shen Qingdai is the first disciple driven by curiosity, but she will not be the last.
Su Mujin came over and said softly: "Shen Qingdai is the granddaughter of the elder of the Dan Hall. Her research on matching ratios in the Dan Hall is very good, but because she studies fields that are ineffective for mortals, she has never been taken seriously. What you just said, she will probably think about it for a long time when she goes back."
Qin Chuan nodded and wrote the first line of notes in his workbook: "Shen Qingdai - spiritual power concentration ratio - may become the docking person for the research and development of medicine for mortals."
After writing, he put down his pen and looked out the window at the medicinal field. Those lush herbs swayed in the sun, each one containing possibilities that the monks could not fully release. His job is not to create from scratch, but to translate these possibilities into language that mortals can use. The essence of information gap is not to show off knowledge, but to fill blind spots. His value in Baicao Valley is not that he is Su Mujin's guest or that he is the registered disciple of the Reincarnation Sword Master - but that he can see blind spots that others cannot and is willing to fill them.
In the evening, Shen Qingdai came back. She was holding a thick book in her hand, with "List of Forbidden Medicinal Materials for Mortals" written on the cover. She put the booklet on Qin Chuan's desk and said expressionlessly: "I compiled this. All the elixirs that are known to be ineffective or poisonous to mortals. There are 217 flavors in total. The categories are arranged according to parts, nature, flavor, and toxicity level."
Qin Chuan opened the booklet and saw that the name, nature, flavor, menstruation, toxicity and contraindication reasons of each medicinal ingredient were written in neat small letters, and the specific cases were also noted in small letters next to it. The level of detail in this job is completely different from what a disciple who is "ordered to deal with it" can do.
He looked up at Shen Qingdai. Shen Qingdai turned her head away, the tips of her ears turning slightly red.
"Thanks."
"You're welcome. I just don't want you to randomly test medicine and kill people." She paused and then said, "You can call me if you make any progress."
Then she turned and walked away. Qin Chuan watched her back disappear on the path among the medicine fields, and then looked down at the booklet in his hand. There are two hundred and seventeen medicinal herbs, each one is written clearly. This is not perfunctory, it is the professionalism that a professional pharmacist instinctively bursts out after being touched by the nerve called "I have never thought about this problem."
He closed the book and added another line of notes on the workbook: "Shen Qingdai - available. Need: recognition. Pain point: long-term marginalization of the research field. Breakthrough: give her a visible result."
